html:
Nairobi is the capital of Kenya. It began in 1899 as a depot on the Uganda Railway, at a swampy spot the Maasai called Enkare Nairobi, "cool water".

The British were building the line from Mombasa on the coast to Lake Victoria. Nairobi lay halfway, at the last level ground before the climb into the highlands, so workshops and stores were set up there. It grew fast and in 1905 replaced Mombasa as capital of the British East Africa Protectorate. White settlers took farmland in the highlands around it, while Africans and Indian traders and workers were kept to separate parts of town.

Africans' anger at land loss and segregation fed the Mau Mau rebellion of the 1950s. At independence in 1963 Nairobi became the capital of Jomo Kenyatta's Kenya. In 1972 it was chosen as the home of the United Nations Environment Programme, and it is now a hub of business, technology and aid for East Africa, with millions of people.
sum: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya. It began in 1899 as a depot on the Uganda Railway, at a swampy spot the Maasai called Enkare Nairobi, "cool water".
